title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming
read_level: partial (arXiv HTML: full main text Secs 1-5 and limitations, supplement tool table H; most supplementary tables not read)
why_wsp: GPT-6-Astra inspects both CLIP towers and writes closed-form weight-edit programs (no backprop or iterative fitting), guided by a supplied paired hard-negative statistic D; its recurring output-projection shrink is distilled into an agent-free closed-form recipe (TowerBridge).
editor: Astra (GPT-6-Astra); TowerBridge itself uses no LLM
target: 13 CLIP checkpoints via open_clip in agent sessions (ViT-B/32, B/16, L/14); TowerBridge on 21 CLIP checkpoints incl. ViT-H/14 plus 5 other dual encoders; parameter counts not stated
interface: code/tensor tools (python over weights without gradients, probe, crossmap, evaluate, test); edits restricted to closed-form computations
loop: closed-loop with feedback (agent scores candidates on selection set / COCO val within tool budgets; sealed test sets)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: '12 of the 13 final patches rewrite an output projection' (Sec 4.2); TowerBridge shrinks d/4 directions in both output projections

headline_results.claim: Agent improves COCO test retrieval on all 13 checkpoints, mean +12.2 RSUM
headline_results.quote: Astra's programs improve COCO test retrieval on all 13 checkpoints, each significantly, by +12.2 RSUM on average
The gains extend to Flickr30k test, averaging +5.8 RSUM and reaching significance on 11 of 13 checkpoints
TowerBridge improves COCO test retrieval by 16.8 RSUM and Flickr30k test retrieval by 6.6 on average across all 21 evaluated CLIP checkpoints, including 8 unseen by the agent

headline_results.claim: Random search with same statistic matches agent on Flickr30k test
headline_results.quote: a random search over a fixed edit grammar with the same statistic also finds projection corrections, with a similar mean Flickr30k test gain ( +5.7 against +5.8

headline_results.claim: Removing D hurts more than removing raw-weight reading
headline_results.quote: removing D reduces Flickr30k validation gains by 6.3 and 1.7 RSUM, respectively. Removing raw-weight reading has a smaller effect, 0.5 and 1.3 RSUM.
the median share of text-to-image misses landing on hubs falls from 28% to 19%.

headline_results.claim: TowerBridge beats agent patches on all 13
headline_results.quote: TowerBridge also outperforms the agent's own patches on all 13 checkpoints with a session

cost.claim: Agent tool-call budgets per session: python 300, probe 30, crossmap 20, evaluate 100, test 50 (table values)
cost.quote: The tools let the agent inspect the model, construct an edit and assess its effect within fixed budgets
The recipe takes seconds for each model and requires no agent.

baselines_and_controls: Zero-shot checkpoints; modality-gap removal, centering, all-but-the-top; top principal directions without pair labels; random search over fixed edit grammar with same statistic; controls removing D or raw-weight access; eigenvalue-weighted shrink; re-rankers (CSLS, NNN, QB-Norm, DN) and KISSME.
runs_and_variance: One agent session per checkpoint (13); 95% paired bootstrap CIs grouped by image; controls on two checkpoints with a later harness.
robustness_of_edits: Transfer to Flickr30k (not seen by agent), 8 unseen checkpoints, 5 other dual-encoder families; ImageNet zero-shot drop capped at 0.5 points; no fine-tuning/quantization tests.
verification: static checks: 'We statically check every code block and manually trace each final patch array to its source code; all 13 final patches pass these checks.' (Sec 3.2); first-order optimality proof for bilinear surrogate (Ky Fan)
memorization_vs_reasoning: Random search with the same statistic reached similar Flickr30k gain; removing the supplied statistic D hurt more than removing raw-weight access, suggesting the supplied evidence carries much of the signal.
limitations_stated: Requires labelled image-text pairs; targets dual encoders; trained maps and re-rankers with in-domain bank can achieve larger gains.
code_or_data: none found (authors state 'We will release code, prompts and logs')
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. Sparks of WSP [54]
notes_for_survey: Example of agent WSP sessions used as a discovery step whose recurring edit is distilled into a closed-form, agent-free recipe that outperforms the agent's own patches. Includes the control that random search with the same supplied statistic matches the agent on Flickr30k test.
